key_big: Stress = F/A; strain = ΔL/L; Y = stress/strain.
key_sub: Hooke's law holds up to the limit of proportionality.
body_html:
How to think about it

When a force deforms a body, stress = F/A and strain = ΔL/L. Within the elastic limit stress is proportional to strain (Hooke's law), and the constant is a modulus: Young's modulus Y for stretching, bulk modulus B for change of volume and shear modulus G for twisting. Steel has a larger Y than rubber, so it is more elastic.

The elastic potential energy stored in a stretched wire is ½ × stress × strain × volume. On a stress–strain curve we find the proportional limit, yield point, ultimate strength and fracture point. Poisson's ratio is lateral strain ÷ longitudinal strain.

Example

Stress 2 × 10⁸ Pa, strain 0.001. Y?

stress ÷ strain

Answer: 2 × 10¹¹ Pa

Example

Steel or rubber: more elastic?

larger Y

Answer: steel

Common mistakes

  • Thinking rubber is more elastic than steel.
  • Using the diameter as radius in the area.
  • Forgetting to convert mm² to m².

faq.q: Why is steel more elastic than rubber?
faq.a: For the same stress, steel is strained much less, so its modulus is much greater.
